# Switch NX2 - read when the Lichii GUI starts.
# One NAME=VALUE per line. Lines starting with # are ignored.
# A variable already set in the environment wins over this file.
# Between files, the user copy (%APPDATA%\eden\nx2_switches.txt, or
# $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/eden/nx2_switches.txt) wins over this one, so editing this file is never
# needed: copy the lines you want into your own and restart.
#
# Restart the emulator after editing.

# --- Performance tuning defaults for Switch 2 ---
# Offload GPU method/macro execution to the back thread (SPLIT=2 delivers up to +54% FPS alone).
EDEN_NX2_SPLIT=2

# Batch GPU fence syncpoints to reduce host driver overhead and smooth frametimes.
EDEN_NX2_FENCE_BATCH=1

# Leave buffer downloads disabled on Switch 2 (default): forcing downloads (=1) copies back
# 90-220 MB/s of buffers CPU never touches, causing heavy mutex contention and dropping FPS by ~38-63%.
#EDEN_NX2_BUFFER_DOWNLOADS=1

# Paces frame submission 2 frames ahead. Reduces frametime spikes, but adds ~1-2 frames of input latency.
# Enable only if frame pacing stability is preferred over responsive controls.
#EDEN_NX2_FRAMES_AHEAD=2

# --- Workarounds / Debug ---
# Terrain/indirect drawing fix for Donkey Kong Bananza: enabled by default. Set to 0 only to leave to GPU.
#EDEN_NX2_RESETFIX=0

# Drop reactive-flushing read traps on Switch 2 programs (opt-in; can reduce FPS from 29 to 24 in MKW).
#EDEN_NX2_NO_REACTIVE=1

# Graphics pipelines linked from per-stage shader libraries (VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library with
# fast linking; not on MoltenVK). Off by default; EDEN_NX2_GPL_FAST_LINK=0 links optimized.
#EDEN_NX2_GPL=1

# With EDEN_NX2_GPL=1 and "Precache shaders before game start": the game's vertex and fragment
# programs are also prepared (rebuild the precache after setting it). Ocarina of Time: a 1.5 GB
# file, six more minutes on the first loading screen, 2.3 GB of driver cache; pop-in ends sooner,
# frame times are the same as with the compute precache alone.
#EDEN_NX2_GRAPHICS_PRECACHE=1

# Ocarina of Time with the "AMD FSR 3.1" anti-aliasing choice: 0 draws the scene without the
# per-frame sub-pixel offset FSR is given.
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_JITTER=0

# Ocarina of Time with NVIDIA DLSS (or MetalFX temporal): 1 gives it the same sub-pixel offset,
# 2 with the vertical sign flipped. Experiment, off by default.
#EDEN_NX2_DLSS_JITTER=1

# Ocarina of Time: 1 draws the game's upscale pass as one bilinear tap whenever no temporal
# upscaler takes the frame (phones get it from their device profile; 0 turns it off there).
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_BILINEAR_UPSCALE=1

# Ocarina of Time handheld: 1 lets DLSS / FSR 3.1 take the upscale from the lower scales to
# 1920x1080 (on by default on Apple for MetalFX temporal, 0 turns it off).
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_TEMPORAL_HANDHELD=1

# Ocarina of Time: the 3D scene's size for tests, over the "Resolution" setting (oot_resolution):
# 1 = 75%, 2 = 56%, 3 = 50%, 4 = 40% (768x432 handheld), 5 = 1/3 (640x360 handheld; docked it is
# 40%, since a third of 2560x1440 is padded and drawn twice). The finished picture stays 1920x1080
# handheld. Each change of a frame's sizes writes one "Frame chain:" line.
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_RENDER_SCALE=4

# A draw without render targets (it writes buffers or counts samples only) gets a render pass as
# large as its scissors reach instead of the surface clip (Ocarina of Time leaves that at
# 32768x32768). On by default on Apple, where the GPU prepares every tile of it; 0 turns it off.
#EDEN_NX2_TARGETLESS_REACH=1

# Streamed uniform buffers on MoltenVK: static (default) pads to the shader's used size unless it
# indexes the buffer; readable also zero-fills indexed ones to 64 KiB, bank always 64 KiB, poison
# fills with 0xff the shader can see (finds reads past the guest's size), 0 none.
#EDEN_NX2_UBO_PAD=static

# 0: a fence release submits deferred GPU work only when its callback has not run (something
# waits). Phones get 0 from their device profile.
#EDEN_NX2_RELEASE_SUBMIT=1

# The split GPU thread, out of commands with a deferred submission younger than
# EDEN_NX2_FENCE_FLUSH_US, waits up to this many us for more work first (it spins meanwhile).
#EDEN_NX2_IDLE_GRACE_US=0

# The same wait asleep, and only while the GPU still runs work submitted earlier (it has no use
# for another command buffer yet): up to this many us, ended by new work, by a thread asking for
# the submission or by the GPU running dry (the idea of nxnative PR #2645). 0 = off.
# EDEN_NX2_IDLE_HOLD_ANY=1 holds whatever the GPU does, to measure it on a PC. Phones get 500
# from their device profile (PC phone sim: idle submits 3.0 -> 0.9 a frame, 21.1 -> 19.6 command
# buffers, frame rate unchanged).
#EDEN_NX2_IDLE_HOLD_US=0

# The two GPU threads sleep on each other in the OS's address wait (WaitOnAddress, Apple
# os_sync_wait_on_address) instead of std::atomic::wait, which on Apple polls and yields for up
# to 64 us before it sleeps. 0 = std::atomic::wait.
#EDEN_NX2_SPLIT_ADDRESS_WAIT=1

# 0: the GPU thread polling its suspended channels and a thread waiting for a deferred submission
# sleep 50 us between polls instead of yielding. Phones get 0 from their device profile: Apple's
# sched_yield (swtch_pri) runs the caller at priority 0 for up to 10 ms when anything else is
# runnable, and spins on its core when nothing is. (On Windows a 50 us sleep lasts a timer tick.)
#EDEN_NX2_POLL_YIELD=1

# Apple: frame threads tell the kernel how much CPU time they need each frame
# (THREAD_TIME_CONSTRAINT_POLICY, measured over 120 frames; port of nxnative PR #2569 / #2137).
# A sum of 1 = GPUBack, 2 = GPU, 4 = VulkanWorker, 8 = the guest cores. iPhone and iPad: 7 by
# default; macOS 0. "frame deadlines:" in the Perf host CPU line shows what each declared and how
# often the kernel took it out of the real-time band.
#EDEN_NX2_APPLE_FRAME_DEADLINE=0

# The fencing thread lets a deferred fence submission wait this many us after the fence was
# made before it asks the GPU thread for it (0 = at once).
#EDEN_NX2_FENCE_PATIENCE_US=0

# An emulated mesh draw inside a render pass that began on a command buffer of its own runs its
# compute just before that pass instead of ending and reopening it (when no draw of the pass stored
# to memory and it samples none of the pass's targets). 0 ends the pass as before.
#EDEN_NX2_MESH_BEFORE_PASS=1

# MoltenVK: a guest dispatch right after another one (only bindings between) records no barrier,
# so both share one serial Metal compute encoder (a barrier ends it). Off by default; force applies
# it on every driver, for tests only (not valid Vulkan).
#EDEN_NX2_DISPATCH_CHAIN=1

# Mesh pipelines the driver could build natively take the compute emulation instead: all, or a
# comma list of pipeline hashes. To compare the two (Apple mesh shaders are occupancy bound).
#EDEN_NX2_MESH_EMULATE=all

# Diagnostic: every 10 s a "Dispatch deps" line names the compute dispatches that end an open
# render pass, and whether they bind its images or follow storage writes in it. Draws nothing
# differently.
#EDEN_NX2_DISPATCH_DEPS=1

# Metal renderer: 0 writes no log line for a SIGABRT or an uncaught Objective-C exception (Metal
# aborts the process on a descriptor or call it rejects; the line names the thread and frames).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_ABORT_TRACE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 makes command buffers without per-encoder status, so a failed one logs its
# error without the encoders that did not complete.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_ENCODER_STATUS=0

# Metal renderer: 0 hands Metal the guest's vertex layout, pipeline and texture descriptions as
# they are, as before. Metal aborts the process on some (a 32nd vertex stream or attribute, an
# attribute of a stream without a buffer, a sample count a texture can't have, a texture past its
# size limit, alpha to coverage on an integer target); by default the vertex layout is rewritten
# to what the vertex program reads and what is left over is refused with a "refused:" log line,
# the draw skipped; alpha to coverage is left off on an integer target; a pass without
# attachments says it has one sample per pixel; a buffer, texture or sampler slot past a stage's
# tables is not bound; 1D images are kept as 2D textures a texel high and shaders read them as
# such, as on MoltenVK (Metal's 1D textures take no mip levels and no 2D views); a texture view
# of another family of texture types, with a slice count its type can't have or in a format Metal
# doesn't cast to is refused with a "refused:" log line, as is a 1D or 3D texture in a depth or
# stencil format.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_PIPELINE_CHECK=0

# Threads of a pool of their own ("VkPipelineHeld") for the graphics pipeline builds a draw waits
# for: such a build starts there at once, at the waiting thread's priority (on Apple its QoS
# class), instead of queueing behind the other builds on the low-priority builder pool; a build
# already running there is lent the waiter's QoS (Apple), and the background prebuild pauses while
# a draw waits. 2 by default on Apple, 0 (off, as before) elsewhere.
#EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_HOLD_BOOST=2

# The list of pipelines a game really drew (what the loading screen builds) is written at most
# this many seconds after a pipeline's first use and when the app leaves the foreground, off the
# GPU thread and through a temporary file. 10 by default on MoltenVK; 0 elsewhere: as before, on a
# first use 15 s after the last save and at shutdown.
#EDEN_NX2_USED_PIPELINES_SAVE_S=10

# Test: every graphics pipeline built at run time (not at boot or by the prebuild) takes this many
# ms of CPU time longer, to stand in for a slow driver compiler.
#EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_BUILD_DELAY_MS=300

# Test: threads of the pipeline builder pool, up to the default (logical CPUs - 1; an iPhone 17
# Pro Max has 5).
#EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_WORKERS=5

# MoltenVK times its compilation stages (SPIR-V to MSL, MSL compile, pipeline compile, ...) for
# the "Perf pipelines:" line. 1 by default on iOS, 0 on macOS.
#EDEN_NX2_MVK_STATS=1

#EDEN_NX2_MME_JIT=0
#EDEN_NX2_PBFLUSH=0
#EDEN_NX2_SKIP_SAME=0
#EDEN_NX2_INLINE_DEFER=0
#EDEN_NX2_SPLIT_SKIP=1
#EDEN_NX2_AUTO_STUB=1
#EDEN_NX2_KEEP_ASTC=1

# --- Memory ---
# Windows: guest memory is committed as the game allocates it instead of all at start (about
# 4.5 GiB less commit charge in Ocarina of Time). Set to 0 to commit all of it at start.
#EDEN_NX2_SEC_RESERVE=0

# Cap the texture cache's device memory (MiB) below what the graphics driver's budget allows.
#EDEN_NX2_TC_CEILING_MIB=7680

# --- CPU scheduling ---
# Hex mask of guest cores whose host threads keep the top priority (and on Apple the performance
# cores); the others run one class lower. On a 4-CPU host (2 fast + 2 slow, no pinning) Kokiri
# Forest went from 52-53 to 66-70 fps with 03; no change with all 24 CPUs.
#EDEN_NX2_GUEST_CORE_FIRST=03

# Ocarina of Time: 0 keeps the game's own multi-core masks, 2 narrows each to the thread's ideal
# core (default: widened to every core).
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_WIDE_AFFINITY=0

# Yield backoff: a gap between two yields longer than this (us, default 100) starts a new run;
# with 0, changed callee-saved registers no longer start one. Ocarina of Time changes them at
# every yield, so its backoff never sleeps; making it sleep cost about 60 % of the frame rate.
#EDEN_NX2_YIELD_BACKOFF_GAP_US=100
#EDEN_NX2_YIELD_BACKOFF_REGS=0

# "Perf sched:" line (with EDEN_NX2_PERF_REPORT=1): list the busiest n guest threads (default 5).
#EDEN_NX2_PERF_SCHED_THREADS=5
# 0 drops the "Perf threads:" and "Perf sched:" lines and the counting behind them.
#EDEN_NX2_PERF_SCHED=0

# Guest loads/stores that take the JIT's memory callbacks ("Perf memory callbacks:" line).
# arm64 hosts: 1 runs LDXR/STXR in fastmem (a load and a host CAS) instead of a callback each
# (off by default: Ocarina of Time runs none on the PC; iOS Experiments turns it on).
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_INLINE_EXCLUSIVES=1
# A plain load that faults in fastmem gives fastmem up only at its nth fault (default 0 or 1: at
# the first). Read traps fault once and are then disarmed; on the PC phone sim 8 cut Ocarina of
# Time's GPU-tracked slow loads 14k -> 4k/s, but those left are the flushing reads.
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_LOAD_FAULTS=8
# x64, diagnostic: 1 sends LDXR/STXR through the callbacks and the global monitor, as arm64 did.
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_EXCLUSIVE_CALLBACKS=1
# The reactive flushing setting for this session (0 = read traps, as on iOS and macOS).
#EDEN_NX2_REACTIVE_FLUSHING=0
# Guest reads of a page whose GPU-written bytes are not in guest memory yet ("Perf CPU reads:"
# line: asks, cache lock time, waits by cause, who landed the bytes). 0: the GPU thread copies
# the page again and waits for the GPU to go idle, page by page. 1: a fence download of those
# bytes already in flight is waited for (its own submission only) and landed by the GPU thread,
# with the finished downloads within EDEN_NX2_GPU_READ_LAND_KIB (default 256) of the read.
# 2: also, when that download is already submitted, the reading core waits and lands it itself,
# so the GPU thread keeps recording. Default 2 on Apple hosts, 0 elsewhere. PC phone sim, Ocarina
# of Time in Kokiri: GPU thread held 79 -> 49 -> 5.5 ms/s, GPU-tracked load 13.2 -> 9.7 -> 8.2 us.
#EDEN_NX2_GPU_READ_LAND=0
#EDEN_NX2_GPU_READ_LAND_KIB=256
# Hot pages (Djihads80/Eglantine f27522bfb9): a page the guest writes twice within 128 frames,
# each time after an upload had write-protected it, is no longer protected. It counts as written
# at the end of each epoch instead, so its first use in the next epoch uploads it, and the buffer
# cache's write memos (bind skips, uniform reuse, repacked vertex streams) hear of it then. Pages
# the GPU ever wrote are never hot; all hot pages cool down every 128 frames. 0: off. 1: an epoch
# is a frame (as upstream). 2: an epoch also ends with each guest command list. Default 2 on
# Apple hosts, 0 elsewhere. PC phone sim, Ocarina of Time in Kokiri: GPU-tracked guest stores
# 909k -> 439k/s, tracker protections 17.1k -> 9.7k/s, buffer uploads 97 -> 137 MiB/s, frame
# rate unchanged (1: 475k/s, 10.8k/s, 109 MiB/s). Tracker protect and unprotect counts, and the
# hot page counts, are in the "Perf CPU writes:" line.
#EDEN_NX2_HOT_PAGES=0
# Diagnostics: keep the bytes of each hot page upload and compare them at each later use in the
# epoch ("hot verify: stale" = uses write protection would have uploaded first).
#EDEN_NX2_HOT_PAGES_VERIFY=1
